quest.title: A Gifted Rose: Long Day Ahead
quest.description: The flowers planted by Affan haven't sprouted yet. Water them for him.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Delicious Shawarma Wrap x2, Delicious Tahchin x2, Glabrous Beans x2

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Ah, I haven't had time to cook yet, so I'm afraid I have nothing with which to receive you as guests.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So, this other kid is your friend, huh? She's pretty cute.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Do you want to come see the flowers when they bloom?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: They will most likely bloom in a few days. Come back later to see the flowers you helped to plant.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Alright, I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Come, come, look at these seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Doesn't look like there's been any change.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I've been growing crops for years, but growing flowers must be different.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Why else haven't they grown after so long?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see, hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grandpa Affan, Paimon thinks your nursery is too dry. And there might not be enough nutrients in the soil around Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've helped a villager grow flowers before, so we have experience.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Huh. Is that so...

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: That makes sense. Such rare flowers should be more delicate than normal ones. Indeed, I don't water and fertilize them enough.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: But this nursery is a little far from any water sources. It's not easy to bring water here.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: And I don't store much water for daily use either, so it is rather inconvenient to water the seeds in the nursery often.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can help.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Alright, in that case, please water these three seeds first.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Good, good, you two are very resourceful.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I have a feeling that they will grow well this time, now that I have guidance from the experts.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Were the Shawarma and Tahchin good?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Delicious, eh? I'll make more for you, then.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'm not as good of a cook as my late wife, so forgive my poor cooking. Please take them. The portions are smaller this time, though.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is so tasty! You're really kind! We'll visit you often.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Haha, didn't you children want to ask me what kind of flower this is?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I guess I might as well tell you. I'm planting roses.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: As in, Sumeru Roses?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: This type of flower is called the Golden Rose. It's much more precious than the Sumeru Rose.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Remember how I told you that these flower seeds were left to me by a friend?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Well, these seeds, and this old house I'm living in now were all left to me by that late "old ghost."

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Oh, I forgot. You're not from Aaru Village, so you're most likely not familiar with that name.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: No matter. Just think of that fellow as an old man who used to grow some flowers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Grandpa Affan, you're spacing out all of a sudden. Hello! Hello?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Ah! Oh. I was lost in thought. I'm sorry, I'm old, and my mind has begun to wander. How embarrassing...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Thank you again, children. You can have a look around if there's anything else you want to see.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I won't drive people away anymore. But be careful not to tread on the nursery.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Water these three seeds first, and I'll think about what to do about the fertilizer.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: After growing things for decades, I do know how to make some simple fertilizer.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: ♪Rose, oh rose, grant me my wish...

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Hmm? You're still here?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Well, anyway, I'm an old weirdo, and "old weirdos behave in inexplicable ways." Few people ask me questions like you do.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've always wanted to go out and grab the chance to do something with my life.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: When I was a newlywed, I almost left with the Eremites, but then I thought about it, and I couldn't just leave my wife to take up a life of wandering.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Later, I met a traveling merchant and wanted to follow suit and do some business, but that didn't work out because I didn't have enough Mora.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Much later, my wife passed and nothing held me back anymore, but by then, I'd gotten too old to leave.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've dragged things out up till now and I've missed out on too much.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: In retrospect, I've found that I belong neither to this village, nor to anywhere else.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So in the end, I moved by myself to the edge of the village, and I found life here to be more comfortable.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: And decades went by, just like that.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'd like to invite you to come and see these flowers when they bloom. It's probably going to be tomorrow or the day after. Will you be able to make it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Alright, alright...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: ♪Rose, oh rose, grant me my wish...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Only outsiders ask about the old ghost. The children of the village all know his name.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Whenever a child is naughty, their parents will say, "The old ghost will come take you away."

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: These younglings don't know the old ghost at all, but are pretty good at using his name to scare people.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I met the old ghost myself as a child. He did dislike children, but he wasn't scary.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: For some reason, he became known as the old ghost. I thought it was just a bunch of people talking about him behind his back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Weren't you friends?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: When I was young, I used to sneak close to his garden to play. He'd chase me away with a garden hoe as soon as he saw me.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He probably took me for a naughty child looking to cause trouble. Why would he remember me?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He might not have known who I was, but I still remember him and his little garden.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So I suppose I can call him my friend, right?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I want to grow the same flowers, just to recreate that little garden in my memories.
